question: Srimanta Sankardev is generally acknowledged with pioneering new musical, dramatic, and linguistic forms. He is associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Srimanta Sankardev (1449–1568) was a great saint, scholar, poet, playwright and social reformer of Assam, and the founder of the Ekasarana Dharma (Neo-Vaishnavite) movement.

• He created the classical dance form Sattriya, which developed in the Sattras (Vaishnava monasteries) of Assam as a medium of devotion and storytelling.

• Sattriya was formally recognised as a classical dance of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000, making it the eighth classical dance form.

• Sankardev also introduced:

◦ Ankia Naat – one-act devotional plays; and Bhaona – their stage performance.

◦ Borgeet – devotional songs; and Kirtan Ghosha, his major literary work.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Manipuri is the classical dance of Manipur, famous for the Raas Leela of Radha and Krishna.

• Kathakali is the classical dance-drama of Kerala, known for its elaborate make-up and masks.

• Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha, whose sculpturesque poses derive from temple carvings.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

• Majuli, the largest river island in the world (in Assam), is the main centre of the Sattra culture founded by Sankardev.

question: Which of the following singer is the recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asha Bhosle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Asha Bhosle, the legendary playback singer, received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for the year 2000.

• She has also been honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2008) and holds a Guinness World Record for recording the most songs in music history.

• The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in the field of cinema, given annually by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting at the National Film Awards.

◦ It was instituted in 1969, the birth centenary year of Dhundiraj Govind Phalke (Dadasaheb Phalke), the "Father of Indian Cinema".

◦ The first recipient was the actress Devika Rani (1969).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dadasaheb Phalke made India's first full-length feature film, "Raja Harishchandra", in 1913.

• Other singers who received the award: Lata Mangeshkar (1989) and Bhupen Hazarika (1992).

• Sonu Nigam, Neha Kakkar and Arijit Singh are well-known playback singers but have not received this award.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (highest honour in cinema) with the Bharat Ratna (highest civilian award) — Lata Mangeshkar received both, the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

• The award carries a Swarna Kamal (Golden Lotus), a cash prize and a shawl.

question: According to the Union Home Ministry, the census 2021 (which got postponed due to COVID 19) was supposed to collect data for ______ for the first time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Other Backward Castes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs, the Census 2021 was to collect data on Other Backward Classes (OBCs) for the first time in independent India's census exercise.

• The Census was postponed because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

• Data on Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) has been collected in every census since 1951, so it would not have been a 'first time'.

• Census 2021 was also planned to be India's first digital census, with a mobile app for data collection and a self-enumeration facility.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The last caste-wise enumeration of all castes in British India was in 1931.

• The Census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948, by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, which works under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

• Census is a Union subject listed at entry 69 of the Union List and is mentioned in Article 246 of the Constitution.

NOTE

• The Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953) was the first backward classes commission, and the B. P. Mandal Commission (1979) recommended 27% reservation for OBCs, implemented in 1990.

• The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) was given constitutional status by the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018 (Article 338B).

question: The total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall not exceed ______ percent of the total number of members of the House of the People.
solution_text:
The correct answer is fifteen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 75(1A) of the Constitution provides that the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

• This ceiling was inserted by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, to curb the practice of forming oversized ministries.

◦ The same amendment fixed the same 15% limit for States under Article 164(1A), with a minimum of 12 Ministers in a State.

◦ It also provided that a member disqualified on the ground of defection cannot be appointed a Minister.

• Since the Lok Sabha has 543 elected members, the ceiling works out to about 81 Ministers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 74 – there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President; such advice is binding on the President (as clarified by the 42nd and 44th Amendments).

• Article 75 – the Prime Minister is appointed by the President, and the other Ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.

• The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)).

NOTE

• The Council of Ministers has three ranks: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers.

• A Minister who is not a member of either House must become a member of Parliament within six months (Article 75(5)).

question: "Brahmadeya" a type of land during Chola Period was the ______.
option_2: land of non - Brahmana peasant proprietors
solution_text:
The correct answer is land gifted to Brahmans.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Brahmadeya" literally means "given to Brahmanas", and it referred to land granted (usually tax-free) to Brahmanas by kings and chiefs during the Chola period and in early medieval South India.

• Such grants were recorded on copper plates and stone inscriptions and often carried exemption from taxes.

• A settlement of Brahmanas holding such land was called an agrahara, and its assembly was the sabha (or Brahmadeya sabha).

• Other Chola land categories:

◦ Vellanvagai – land of non-Brahmana peasant proprietors.

◦ Devadana / Tirunamattukkani – land gifted to temples.

◦ Pallichchhandam – land donated to Jaina institutions.

◦ Shalabhoga – land for the maintenance of a school.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Chola local self-government was famous for its village assemblies: the ur (assembly of ordinary villages), the sabha (of Brahmadeya villages) and the nagaram (of merchants).

• The Uttaramerur inscription of Parantaka I gives detailed information about the election procedure (kudavolai system) of village assemblies.

NOTE

• Famous Chola rulers: Vijayalaya (founder), Rajaraja I (built the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur) and Rajendra I (took the title Gangaikonda Chola after his northern campaign).

• Chola temples of the "Great Living Chola Temples" group are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

question: Which of the following structure is associated with Buddhism?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stupa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Stupa" is a hemispherical (dome-shaped) structure built over the relics of the Buddha or a Buddhist monk, and it is the most characteristic monument of Buddhist architecture.

• Main parts of a stupa:

◦ Anda – the hemispherical dome; Harmika – the square railing on top; Yashti – the central mast; Chhatra – the umbrella crowning it.

◦ Medhi – the raised drum/base; Pradakshina Patha – the circumambulatory path; Torana – the ornamental gateways.

• Emperor Ashoka is said to have built a large number of stupas; the Great Stupa at Sanchi (Madhya Pradesh), originally built by Ashoka, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Pallava" is the name of a South Indian dynasty (famous for Mahabalipuram), not a structure.

• Option 2 "Mandapa" is the pillared hall in front of the sanctum of a Hindu temple.

• Option 3 "Shikhara" is the rising tower over the sanctum in the Nagara style of Hindu temple architecture (called Vimana in the Dravida style).

NOTE

• Other Buddhist architectural forms: Chaitya (prayer hall) and Vihara (monastery/residence of monks) — as seen at Ajanta, Ellora, Karle and Bhaja.

• Important stupas: Sanchi (MP), Bharhut (MP), Amaravati (Andhra Pradesh), Dhamek at Sarnath (UP) and Kesariya (Bihar).

question: Which of the famous personalities belonged to the extremist phase of modern history?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Extremist phase (1905–1919) of the Indian national movement was led by the trio Lal–Bal–Pal — Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal — along with Aurobindo Ghosh.

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave the slogan "Swaraj is my birth right and I shall have it" and was called "Lokmanya"; the British termed him the "Father of Indian Unrest".

• The Extremists believed in self-reliance, swadeshi, boycott, national education and passive resistance, unlike the Moderates who relied on prayers, petitions and protests.

• The Surat Split of 1907 formally divided the Congress into Moderates and Extremists; the two groups reunited at the Lucknow Session of 1916.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Pherozeshah Mehta (P. M. Mehta) and Gopal Krishna Gokhale were leading Moderates; Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society (1905) and was Gandhiji's political guru.

• A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, founded the Indian National Congress in 1885; its first session was held in Bombay under the presidency of W. C. Bonnerjee.

NOTE

• Phases of the national movement: Moderate phase (1885–1905), Extremist phase (1905–1919) and Gandhian phase (1919–1947).

• The Partition of Bengal (1905) by Lord Curzon triggered the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement, which marked the rise of the Extremists.

question: Santhal community is an ethnic group of ______ India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is eastern.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Santhals (Santals) are an ethnic tribal community of eastern India, found mainly in Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Bihar and Assam.

• They are the largest tribal community in India in terms of population among the Scheduled Tribes of eastern India.

• They speak Santhali, a language of the Austroasiatic (Munda) family, written in the Ol Chiki script devised by Pandit Raghunath Murmu; Santhali was included in the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.

• The Santhal Rebellion (Santhal Hul) of 1855–56 was led by the brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu against moneylenders, zamindars and the British.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Popular Santhal dances and festivals: Sohrai, Baha and the Karam festival; Dasai dance is also performed by the community.

• Other major tribes of eastern/central India: Munda, Ho, Oraon, Bhumij, Kharia and Gond.

NOTE

• Tribal groups by region: Gond, Bhil (central India), Toda, Chenchu (south), Bhotia, Gujjar (north), Naga, Khasi, Garo, Mizo (north-east) and Jarawa, Onge, Sentinelese (Andaman & Nicobar).

• Article 342 empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Tribes of a State or Union Territory.

question: Chapchar kut festival, is a famous festival of ______ state of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chapchar Kut is the most important and popular festival of Mizoram, celebrated in the month of March.

• It is a spring festival observed after the completion of the jhum (shifting cultivation) clearing operation — that is, after the bamboo and trees felled for cultivation have been left to dry.

• The highlight of the festival is the famous Cheraw dance (bamboo dance), in which dancers move between bamboo staves beaten in rhythm.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Mizoram: Mim Kut (maize festival, celebrated in August–September) and Pawl Kut (harvest festival, December–January).

• Aizawl is the capital of Mizoram; the state became a full-fledged State in 1987 (along with Arunachal Pradesh) under the 53rd Constitutional Amendment Act.

• Mizoram has one of the highest literacy rates in India.

NOTE

• Festivals of the North-East worth remembering: Bihu (Assam), Hornbill Festival (Nagaland), Losoong (Sikkim), Wangala and Nongkrem (Meghalaya), Yaoshang and Sangai Festival (Manipur), Chapchar Kut (Mizoram) and Solung (Arunachal Pradesh).

question: Neeraj Chopra, Clinched the historic gold at Tokyo Olympics 2020 with a throw of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 87.58 m.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Neeraj Chopra won the gold medal in the men's javelin throw at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021) with a best throw of 87.58 m.

• It was India's first Olympic gold medal in athletics and only the second individual Olympic gold for India — after Abhinav Bindra's shooting gold at Beijing 2008.

• Neeraj Chopra hails from Khandra village, Panipat, Haryana, and is a Subedar in the Indian Army (4 Rajputana Rifles).

• He had earlier won gold at the Asian Games 2018 (Jakarta) and the Commonwealth Games 2018 (Gold Coast).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He was conferred the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (2021) — India's highest sporting honour — and the Arjuna Award (2018).

• India won a total of 7 medals at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (1 gold, 2 silver, 4 bronze) — its best-ever Olympic performance at that time.

• 7 August, the day he won the gold, is celebrated in India as National Javelin Day.

NOTE

• The Tokyo Olympics 2020 were postponed to 2021 because of the COVID-19 pandemic but retained the name "Tokyo 2020".

• India's other Olympic gold medals have all come in men's field hockey (8 golds).

question: Which articles of the Indian constitution address fundamental rights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 12 to 35.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III of the Constitution, from Article 12 to Article 35.

• Part III is often called the "Magna Carta of India", and the idea was borrowed from the Constitution of the USA (Bill of Rights).

• The six Fundamental Rights presently available are:

◦ Right to Equality – Articles 14–18

◦ Right to Freedom – Articles 19–22

◦ Right against Exploitation – Articles 23–24

◦ Right to Freedom of Religion – Articles 25–28

◦ Cultural and Educational Rights – Articles 29–30

◦ Right to Constitutional Remedies – Articles 32–35

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Articles 5 to 11 (Part II) deal with Citizenship.

• Articles 36 to 51 (Part IV) contain the Directive Principles of State Policy, borrowed from Ireland.

• Article 51A (Part IVA) lists the Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

NOTE

• Article 12 defines the "State", and Article 13 provides that laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void — the basis of judicial review.

• The Right to Education (Article 21A) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, for children aged 6 to 14 years.

question: The SI unit of power of lens is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is dioptre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The power of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length in metres: P = 1/f (in metres).

• Its SI unit is the dioptre (D), where 1 D = 1 m⁻¹.

◦ A convex (converging) lens has positive power; a concave (diverging) lens has negative power.

◦ Example: a convex lens of focal length 50 cm (0.5 m) has a power of +2 D.

◦ Power measures the degree of convergence or divergence of light produced by the lens, which is why spectacle prescriptions are written in dioptres.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "candela (cd)" is the SI unit of luminous intensity.

• Option 2 "mole (mol)" is the SI unit of the amount of substance.

• Option 3 "watt (W)" is the SI unit of power (rate of doing work), i.e. joule per second — not the power of a lens.

NOTE

• The seven SI base units: metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time), ampere (electric current), kelvin (temperature), mole (amount of substance) and candela (luminous intensity).

• Defects of vision: myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected by a concave lens, and hypermetropia (long-sightedness) by a convex lens.

question: Shifting Agriculture is also known as Jhum in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shifting cultivation is called "Jhum(ing)" in Assam and the other North-Eastern states of India.

• In this method a patch of forest is cleared and burnt (slash-and-burn), crops are grown on the ash-enriched soil for two or three years, and the plot is then abandoned so that it can recover its fertility.

• It is a primitive, subsistence type of farming practised mainly by tribal communities on hill slopes.

• Local names of shifting cultivation in India:

◦ Jhum – Assam and North-East India

◦ Podu / Penda – Andhra Pradesh and Odisha

◦ Bewar / Dahiya / Mashan – Madhya Pradesh

◦ Kumari – Western Ghats; Watra – Rajasthan; Khil – Uttar Pradesh

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• International names: Milpa (Mexico and Central America), Ladang (Indonesia and Malaysia), Ray (Vietnam), Chena (Sri Lanka), Roca (Brazil) and Masole (Congo).

• Disadvantages: deforestation, soil erosion, loss of soil fertility and low productivity.

NOTE

• Other farming types often asked: intensive subsistence farming (Ganga plains), commercial grain farming, plantation agriculture (tea, coffee, rubber) and mixed farming.

• Assam's capital is Dispur, and the state is the largest tea producer in India.

question: Who among the following freedom fighters was one of the founders of the Fergusson College in Pune in 1885?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fergusson College, Pune, was founded in 1885 by the Deccan Education Society, whose founding members included Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, Vishnushastri Chiplunkar and Mahadev Ballal Namjoshi.

• The college was named after Sir James Fergusson, the then Governor of Bombay, who supported the project.

• Earlier, in 1880, the same group had founded the New English School in Pune, and Tilak started the newspapers "Kesari" (Marathi) and "Maratha" (English) in 1881.

• The aim was to provide quality, affordable, indigenous education to Indians and to build national consciousness.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale taught at Fergusson College and later founded the Servants of India Society (1905).

• Subhas Chandra Bose founded the Forward Bloc (1939) and led the Azad Hind Fauj (INA).

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the "Iron Man of India", led the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) and integrated the princely states as India's first Home Minister.

• Lala Lajpat Rai, called "Punjab Kesari", founded the Punjab National Bank and the Lakshmi Insurance Company.

NOTE

• Tilak wrote Gita Rahasya and The Arctic Home in the Vedas, and with Annie Besant launched the Home Rule Movement (1916).

• Educational institutions and founders often asked: Aligarh (MAO College, 1875) – Sir Syed Ahmad Khan; Banaras Hindu University (1916) – Madan Mohan Malaviya; Visva-Bharati (1921) – Rabindranath Tagore.

question: In which sport did Mirabai Chanu win India's first Gold Medal at the Commonwealth Games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Weightlifting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Saikhom Mirabai Chanu won India's first gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2022 (Birmingham) in weightlifting, in the women's 49 kg category.

• She lifted a Games record total of 201 kg (88 kg snatch + 113 kg clean and jerk).

• She had earlier won the silver medal at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 in the same category — India's first medal of those Games.

• She belongs to Manipur and has been honoured with the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (2018), the Padma Shri (2018) and the Arjuna Award.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mirabai Chanu also won gold at the World Weightlifting Championships in 2017 (Anaheim, USA) and at the Commonwealth Games 2018 (Gold Coast).

• The Commonwealth Games 2022 were held at Birmingham, England, where India won 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze) and finished fourth in the medal tally.

NOTE

• Weightlifting has two lifts: the snatch and the clean and jerk; the total of the best of each decides the ranking.

• The Commonwealth Games are held every four years; the first edition was in 1930 at Hamilton, Canada, as the British Empire Games.

question: The government launched the Stand-Up India scheme to promote entrepreneurship among ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Women and SC/ST communities.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Stand-Up India Scheme was launched on 5 April 2016 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi from Noida, Uttar Pradesh.

• It is implemented by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.

• Objective: to promote entrepreneurship among Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST) and women.

◦ It provides bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore for setting up a greenfield (new) enterprise in manufacturing, services, trading or activities allied to agriculture.

◦ Every bank branch is expected to facilitate at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower.

◦ The borrower must be above 18 years of age, and for non-individual enterprises 51% of the shareholding must be held by an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The scheme is operated through the Stand-Up India portal (www.standupmitra.in) with handholding support from SIDBI and NABARD.

• Do not confuse it with Start-up India, also launched in 2016, which supports innovation-driven start-ups across all categories.

NOTE

• Related credit schemes: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (2015) — Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000–₹5 lakh) and Tarun (₹5–10 lakh) loans; and PM SVANidhi (2020) for street vendors.

question: The National Anti-Doping Bill was passed in the Lok Sabha on July 27, 2022. Which of the following organisation manage and administer doping control programs in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) is the national organisation responsible for promoting, coordinating and monitoring the doping control programme in sports in India.

• It was established on 24 November 2005 as a registered society under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

• The National Anti-Doping Bill, 2021 was passed by the Lok Sabha on 27 July 2022 and by the Rajya Sabha on 3 August 2022; it gives statutory backing to NADA and the National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL).

◦ The Act also provides for a National Board for Anti-Doping in Sports to oversee NADA's activities.

◦ It brings India's anti-doping framework in line with the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) code and the UNESCO International Convention against Doping in Sport.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL), New Delhi, is the testing laboratory — it analyses samples but does not manage the overall doping control programme.

• The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) was founded in 1999 and has its headquarters at Montreal, Canada.

NOTE

• "Doping" means the use of prohibited performance-enhancing substances or methods by athletes.

• The Sports Authority of India (SAI) was set up in 1984 for the promotion of sports; the Khelo India programme was launched in 2018.

question: The head office of National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development is located in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) has its head office in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

• It was established on 12 July 1982 on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee, under the NABARD Act, 1981.

• NABARD is the apex development bank for agriculture and rural development in India.

◦ It provides refinance to Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Cooperative Banks and other rural financial institutions.

◦ It supervises RRBs and Cooperative Banks (while the RBI regulates them).

◦ It runs the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), established in 1995–96.

◦ It promotes the Self Help Group (SHG)–Bank Linkage Programme, launched in 1992.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Head offices of other institutions: RBI – Mumbai (established 1935, nationalised 1949), SEBI – Mumbai (1988; statutory in 1992), SIDBI – Lucknow (1990), EXIM Bank – Mumbai (1982), NHB – New Delhi (1988).

• The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme was introduced in 1998 on the initiative of NABARD and RBI.

NOTE

• NABARD took over the functions of the Agricultural Credit Department and Rural Planning and Credit Cell of the RBI and of the Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation (ARDC).

• Its capital is now wholly held by the Government of India.

question: What is added to toothpaste to reduce tooth decay?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fluoride.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fluoride compounds (such as sodium fluoride and sodium monofluorophosphate) are added to toothpaste to prevent tooth decay (dental caries).

• Fluoride converts the hydroxyapatite of the tooth enamel into fluorapatite, which is harder and much more resistant to attack by the acids produced by mouth bacteria.

• Toothpastes are also basic (alkaline) in nature so that they can neutralise the acid formed in the mouth after eating.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Excess fluoride in drinking water causes fluorosis — dental fluorosis (mottling of teeth) and skeletal fluorosis (bone and joint damage). The permissible limit of fluoride in drinking water is about 1.0–1.5 mg/litre.

• Deficiency of iron causes anaemia; cobalt is a constituent of vitamin B12; molybdenum is a micronutrient in plants.

NOTE

• Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body, made mainly of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite).

• Other common chemistry-in-daily-life facts: baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), washing soda is sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O), and bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride (CaOCl₂).

question: "The Inheritance of Loss" is written by which of the following authors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kiran Desai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Inheritance of Loss" (published in 2006) was written by Kiran Desai.

• The novel won the Man Booker Prize in 2006, making her one of the youngest women to win the award; it is set largely in Kalimpong, in the foothills of the Himalayas, against the backdrop of the Gorkhaland movement.

• Her first novel was "Hullabaloo in the Guava Orchard" (1998).

• She is the daughter of the noted novelist Anita Desai.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Jhumpa Lahiri wrote "Interpreter of Maladies" (Pulitzer Prize, 2000), "The Namesake" and "The Lowland".

• Amitav Ghosh wrote "The Shadow Lines", "The Glass Palace", "The Hungry Tide" and the Ibis Trilogy; he was the first English-language writer to receive the Jnanpith Award (2018).

• Anita Desai wrote "Fire on the Mountain", "Clear Light of Day" and "In Custody"; she was shortlisted for the Booker Prize three times.

NOTE

• Indian-origin Booker Prize winners: V. S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981, Midnight's Children), Arundhati Roy (1997, The God of Small Things), Kiran Desai (2006) and Aravind Adiga (2008, The White Tiger).

• Geetanjali Shree won the International Booker Prize (2022) for "Tomb of Sand" (Ret Samadhi), translated by Daisy Rockwell.

question: In which of the following regions days and nights are almost equal in length throughout the year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Equatorial region.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the equatorial region (roughly 0° to 10° north and south of the Equator), the days and nights are almost equal — about 12 hours each — throughout the year.

• The reason is that the Equator is bisected by the circle of illumination at all times of the year, so the effect of the inclination of the earth's axis (23½°) on day length is negligible there.

• The length of day and night varies more and more as one moves away from the Equator towards the poles; at the poles there are periods of continuous day or night lasting about six months.

• The equatorial climate is also marked by high temperature (about 27°C) throughout the year, heavy convectional rainfall and dense evergreen rainforests (Amazon, Congo, Indonesia).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Days and nights are equal all over the world on the two equinoxes — 21 March (Vernal/Spring Equinox) and 23 September (Autumnal Equinox).

• 21 June is the Summer Solstice (longest day in the Northern Hemisphere) and 22 December the Winter Solstice (shortest day in the Northern Hemisphere).

NOTE

• The changing length of day and night and the seasons are caused by the revolution of the earth combined with the tilt of its axis, not by the earth's rotation alone.

• Equatorial forests are called the "lungs of the earth" because of the enormous quantity of oxygen they release.

question: Kathakali is a classical dance of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kathakali is the famous classical dance-drama of Kerala, whose name literally means "story-play" (katha = story, kali = play).

• Its themes are drawn mainly from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

• Distinctive features:

◦ Elaborate make-up (chutti) and costumes, with faces painted in codes such as Pacha (green — noble characters), Kathi (knife — villainous but heroic) and Thadi (bearded characters).

◦ It is traditionally performed by male dancers, who use mudras (hand gestures) and facial expressions instead of speech.

• Famous exponents: Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair, Guru Kunchu Kurup and Kalamandalam Gopi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mohiniyattam is the other classical dance of Kerala, performed solo by women.

• Kuchipudi belongs to Andhra Pradesh, Bharatanatyam to Tamil Nadu, and Yakshagana is a famous folk theatre form of Karnataka.

NOTE

• Classical dances derive their theory from the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni.

• Other art forms of Kerala: Koodiyattam (recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage), Theyyam, Kalaripayattu (martial art) and the festival Onam.

question: Which of the following statement is 'NOT' correct about "Manures"?
option_1: They can be prepared in the fields
option_2: They do not provide humus to soil
option_3: They are relatively less rich in plant nutrients
solution_text:
The correct answer is They do not provide humus to soil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The statement in Option 2 is NOT correct, because manures do provide humus to the soil — that is in fact their greatest advantage.

◦ Manure is a natural organic substance obtained by the decomposition of plant and animal wastes (cow dung, crop residues, farm waste).

◦ On decomposing it adds humus, which improves soil texture, aeration, water-holding capacity and the activity of soil micro-organisms.

• Why the other statements are correct:

◦ Manures can be prepared in the fields by farmers themselves through composting or vermicomposting — so Option 1 is correct.

◦ Manures are relatively less rich in plant nutrients than fertilisers, and are needed in large quantities — so Option 3 is correct.

◦ Manures are natural substances, unlike fertilisers which are manufactured chemically — so Option 4 is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Fertilisers are inorganic, commercially produced and nutrient-specific — for example urea and ammonium sulphate (nitrogenous), superphosphate (phosphatic) and potash (potassic).

• Excessive use of chemical fertilisers causes soil degradation, water pollution and eutrophication.

NOTE

• Types of manure: compost, vermicompost (prepared using earthworms), green manure (growing plants like dhaincha and ploughing them into the soil) and farmyard manure (FYM).

• Nutrients required by plants: macronutrients (N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S) and micronutrients (Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B, Mo, Cl).

question: In migration the factors which cause people to leave their place of residence or origin are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Push factors.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the study of migration, the factors that compel or force people to leave their place of origin or residence are called "push factors".

◦ Examples of push factors: unemployment, poverty, low wages, lack of health and education facilities, natural disasters (floods, droughts, earthquakes), war, political unrest and social discrimination.

• The factors that attract people towards a new place are called "pull factors".

◦ Examples of pull factors: better job opportunities, higher wages, better living conditions, education and medical facilities, security and a pleasant climate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Types of migration: internal (within a country — rural-to-urban, rural-to-rural, urban-to-urban, urban-to-rural) and international (between countries).

• Immigration = movement into a country; emigration = movement out of a country; in-migration and out-migration are the corresponding internal terms.

• In India, rural-to-urban migration is a major cause of the rapid growth of cities and the formation of slums.

NOTE

• Migration is one of the three components of population change, along with births (natality) and deaths (mortality).

• As per Census 2011, Maharashtra and Delhi were among the largest recipients of migrants, while Uttar Pradesh and Bihar were the largest sources.

question: Which place in the world receives the highest rainfall?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mawsynram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mawsynram, situated in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya, receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world — roughly 11,872 mm (about 467 inches).

• The heavy rainfall is caused by:

◦ The funnel-shaped Khasi Hills, which trap the moisture-laden South-West Monsoon winds coming from the Bay of Bengal.

◦ The forced ascent of the moist air along the hill slopes, producing intense orographic (relief) rainfall.

• Cherrapunji (Sohra), also in Meghalaya and only a few kilometres away, is the second wettest place and holds records for the highest rainfall in a single month and year.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Agartala is the capital of Tripura, Guwahati is the largest city of Assam, and Itanagar is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh — all receive heavy but comparatively lower rainfall.

• The capital of Meghalaya is Shillong, known as the "Scotland of the East".

• The name Meghalaya itself means "the abode of clouds".

NOTE

• The driest place in India is Jaisalmer (Rajasthan), in the rain-shadow/arid zone of the Thar Desert.

• The Western Ghats also receive very heavy orographic rainfall on their windward (western) side, while the Deccan Plateau lies in the rain shadow.
